metaData.title: Great Lakes Museum Alliance reporting review

sentences.text: Morning. This is the reporting session we put in after the last quarterly, so it is all yours.
Morning. I have a list, and I am afraid most of it is the same list I had in July.
Then let us go through it properly rather than politely. What is at the top?
The board pack, which I build once a month from four separate pulls out of the system.
Once a report runs past about ten thousand records the file comes back short, and nothing on it tells us it stopped early.
I only know it has happened because I total the file against the count on the screen before I use it.
The first time I missed that check I put a number in front of eleven trustees that was wrong by nine thousand people.
I remember that one. That was February, was it not?
February, and I have checked every file since without exception.
It adds twenty minutes to a job that should not need checking at all, and it means a junior cannot be given the job.
So what I am hearing is that exports are cutting off silently past ten thousand records and your team stitches the files together by hand afterwards.
I want to be sure I am describing it the way you would describe it, because I will be repeating it.
That is close. We do not stitch them together so much as run the same pull three times with different filters.
Each one comes back under the limit that way, and then I put the three together in a spreadsheet.
That is a meaningful difference and I am glad I checked. Three pulls and a spreadsheet, not one pull and a repair.
Three pulls and a spreadsheet. It takes about an hour and a half a month.
Noted with the figure. What is next on the list?
The visitor numbers, and this one is a request rather than a complaint.
We are being asked to show member visits against non member visits by site, and we cannot get that without going to each museum individually.
Eleven museums means eleven emails and eleven different spreadsheet layouts coming back, and two of them always arrive late.
Is that because the visit data lives in the ticketing systems at each site rather than with you?
Exactly that, and I accept it is partly our own architecture rather than yours.
I mention it because if there were ever a sensible way to bring it in, it would save eleven emails a month.
I will note it as context rather than a request, and say so when I write it up.
That is fair. The export one is the real item and it has been the real item since February.
It is on the account and I will add this morning's numbers to it, the hour and a half and the three pulls.
Anything else before I let you go?
No, that is the list. Thank you for sitting through it again.
